'''''Ranunculus muricatus''''' is a species of [[Ranunculus|buttercup]] known by the common names '''rough-fruited buttercup'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''spinyfruit buttercup'''.<ref>{{PLANTS|id=RAMU2|taxon=Ranunculus muricatus|accessdate=18 October 2015}}</ref> It is native to [[Europe]], but it can be found in many other places in the world, including parts of [[Africa]], [[Australia]], and the western and eastern [[United States]], as an [[introduced species]] and agricultural and roadside weed. It grows in wet habitats, such as [[Irrigation|irrigation ditches]]. It is an annual or sometimes biennial herb producing a mostly hairless stem up to half a meter long which may grow erect or decumbent along the ground. The leaves have blades a few centimetres in length which are deeply divided into three lobes or split into three leaflets. They are hairless to hairy in texture, and are borne at the tips of long [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. The flower has five shiny yellow petals under {{convert|1|cm|1}} long around a lobed central receptacle studded with many [[stamen]]s and [[gynoecium|pistils]]. The fruit is a spiny [[achene]] borne in a spherical cluster of 10 to 20.
